title: Arizona DACA Renewals Now Take Five to Six Months as Delays Cost Jobs and Licences
excerpt: Arizona advocates say renewal waits have stretched from about two months to five or six months under new USCIS screening and biometrics requirements. CBS News reports the national backlog of pending renewals has passed 125,000.
body:
• Arizona DACA recipients are waiting five to six months or longer for renewals that previously took about two months, and often less than a month, according to the Arizona Dream Act Coalition.
  • USCIS data shows median renewal wait times jumped from two weeks in 2025 to more than two months in 2026 — the highest, Democratic lawmakers say, since 2016.
  • Advocates attribute the slowdown to near-universal new biometrics requirements and tougher screening; some applicants who filed as far back as November were still unprocessed months later.
  • If your DACA renewal is pending: file as early as the window allows, keep proof of timely filing with you, and tell your employer before your EAD expires — an expired permit means you cannot legally work until the renewal is approved.

DACA recipients in Arizona are facing growing uncertainty as renewal processing stretches to five or six months, leaving some without valid work permits and driver licences while their cases sit pending, the Arizona Republic reported, in coverage republished by Latino Times.

"We are receiving calls every day from people who say they are not receiving their DACA authorization on time," said Anita Enciso, program director at the Arizona Dream Act Coalition, an advocacy group that helps people with DACA applications and renewals. Before the current administration implemented its changes, most renewals took about two months and often less than a month, Enciso said; now recipients wait five to six months or longer, and some who applied as far back as November still had not been processed.

What changed at USCIS

Data from US Citizenship and Immigration Services shows median wait times for DACA renewals jumped from two weeks in 2025 to more than two months in 2026. Democratic lawmakers say wait times are at their highest since 2016, when technical issues disrupted the renewal system.

Enciso said USCIS rarely required renewal applicants to submit new biometric information in the past, but under screening and vetting implemented in 2025, nearly all renewal applicants are being asked for updated biometrics, adding to delays. USCIS has also stopped accepting personal checks or money orders for the renewal fees — $555 to apply online or $605 by mail, plus an $85 biometrics fee — with only cards or direct bank payments now accepted, she said. USCIS is not processing new DACA applications while the programme's legality is contested in court.

USCIS spokesman Zach Kahler said the agency is "safeguarding the American people by more thoroughly screening and vetting all aliens," and added that DACA does not confer legal status and that recipients are not automatically protected from deportation.

The cost of a lapsed permit

The consequences of an expired authorisation are immediate. "If somebody's DACA authorization expires, and someone's work permit expires, that leaves them unable to work," said Julia Gelatt, associate director of the US Immigration Policy Program at the Migration Policy Institute. Employers, she added, are increasingly jittery about keeping employees whose work permits are not valid. Advocates say the delays are also costing recipients their driver licences.

The Arizona picture matches a national one: CBS News has reported that the backlog of pending DACA renewals has grown to more than 125,000 cases, that the number of active DACA holders fell 14% between September 2025 and June 2026, and that USCIS now says it adjudicates 80% of renewals within seven months — while advising recipients to apply only four to five months before expiration. Arizona is home to between 16,000 and 20,000 DACA recipients, according to Arizona PBS's Horizonte programme, where Aliento founder Reyna Montoya and immigration attorney Delia Salvatierra described recipients unable to work, drive, or take their children to school while renewals pend.

What to watch

Whether USCIS processing times recover, and whether Congress takes up the long-term fix advocates are demanding, will decide if the delays are a backlog or a new normal. Renewal filing guidance and fee information are on the Arizona reporting summarised by Latino Times; recipients facing a lapse should contact a local legal aid organisation before their permit expires, not after.
